claims.text: The targeted property in fcc Fe-Co-Ni-based high-entropy alloys is the strength-ductility combination, especially under cryogenic conditions.
The current primary scientific challenge is the lack of a direct correlation between orbital magnetic moment and stacking fault energy.
Stacking fault energy governs the transition from dislocation slip to mechanical twinning.
CoCrFeMnNi is an fcc Fe-Co-Ni-based high-entropy alloy.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi forms a chemically disordered fcc solid solution at ambient pressure.
The relevant fcc alloys are characterized by high configurational entropy.
Changing Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni ratios can tune the orbital magnetic moment contribution.
Stacking fault energy in fcc high-entropy alloys depends on composition.
Co and Cr decrease stacking fault energy, whereas Fe and Ni increase it.
Below 100 K, these alloys exhibit a transition from dislocation slip to mechanical twinning.
Fcc CoCrFeMnNi exhibits transitions from paramagnetism to a spin-glass state and then to ferromagnetism at approximately 93 K and 38 K.
Local chemical ordering may place Cr preferentially on face-centered positions and Co or Ni on cube-corner positions.
Stacking fault energy and local chemical ordering are influenced by lattice distortion and magnetic interactions.
The orbital magnetic moment affects electronic-structure stability and thereby modulates stacking fault energy.
Specific orbital-moment configurations stabilize or destabilize stacking faults and consequently control mechanical twinning versus dislocation slip.
Mechanical twinning enhances ductility, whereas dislocation slip enhances strength in these alloys.
The orbital-moment effect cannot currently be decoupled from lattice-distortion and chemical-disorder effects on stacking fault energy.
Optimizing orbital-moment contributions through Co, Ni, Fe, and Cr ratios will tune stacking fault energy and maximize cryogenic strength-ductility synergy.
Cryogenic strength-ductility enhancement in current fcc high-entropy alloys is attributed primarily to lattice distortion and configurational entropy.
The proposed mechanism applies only to fcc single-phase Fe-Co-Ni-Cr-Mn solid solutions and may not apply to BCC or substantially intermetallic alloys.
